exercises.prompt: Rewrite in a formal written register, starting with 'The survey' and using the passive of 'carry out' and 'owing to': We didn't do the survey because we ran out of money.

accept: The survey was not carried out owing to lack of funds.
The survey was not carried out owing to insufficient funds.
The survey was not carried out owing to a lack of funding.
The survey was not carried out owing to lack of funding.
The survey was not carried out owing to insufficient funding.
The survey was not carried out owing to a shortage of funds.
The survey was not carried out owing to financial constraints.

The survey was not carried out owing to budgetary constraints.

The survey could not be carried out owing to insufficient funds.

The survey could not be carried out owing to budget constraints.

The survey was not carried out owing to limited funds.
The survey was not carried out owing to a shortage of funding.
The survey could not be carried out owing to the lack of funds.
The survey could not be carried out owing to limited funds.
The survey could not be carried out owing to lack of funding.
The survey could not be carried out owing to insufficient funding.

The survey could not be carried out owing to budgetary constraints.
exercises.explanation_ru: Формальный вариант строится на пассиве с carry out и предложной причине owing to + существительное вместо разговорного придаточного because we ran out of money.

exercises.prompt: This study ___ (informal: looks into) how social media use affects teenagers' sleep. Two hundred ___ (informal: kids) aged 13 to 17 kept a sleep diary for four weeks. The findings ___ (informal: kind of show) that heavy use before bedtime is associated with shorter sleep. ___ (informal: But), the sample was small, and the results should be interpreted with ___ (informal: being careful).
exercises.explanation_ru: Академический регистр: латинский глагол вместо фразового (examines), нейтральное существительное вместо kids (adolescents, participants), осторожный глагол-доклад (suggest), формальная связка (However) и номинализация (with caution).

exercises.prompt:
A: Have you seen my keys anywhere?
B: ___ in the car?
exercises.explanation_ru: Разговорный эллипсис убирает вспомогательный и подлежащее вместе: (Have you) Left them in the car? Форма причастия при этом сохраняется. Have left без you — полуобрывок, leaving them спрашивает о другом (оставляешь сейчас?), а did leave — ошибка формы.

exercises.prompt: Which line sounds most like relaxed spoken English rather than writing?
options: She's really sharp, that new intern of yours.
That new intern of yours is really sharp.
Your new intern is exceptionally intelligent.
It is your new intern who is really sharp.
exercises.explanation_ru: «Хвост» — повтор подлежащего в конце (…, that new intern of yours) — примета живой речи: сначала оценка, потом уточнение, о ком речь. Нейтральный порядок годится и для письма, exceptionally intelligent — формальный регистр, а it-конструкция выделяет, кто именно, — это письменный приём контраста.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite as a speaker might say it, putting 'that client in Boston' first as a 'head' and referring back to it with a pronoun: I just can't figure out that client in Boston.
exercises.answer: That client in Boston, I just can't figure him out.
accept: That client in Boston, I just can't figure her out.
That client in Boston, I just can't figure them out.
That client in Boston — I just can't figure him out.
That client in Boston — I just can't figure her out.
That client in Boston — I just can't figure them out.
exercises.explanation_ru: «Голова» выносит тему в начало отдельной группой, а в самом предложении её заменяет местоимение: That client in Boston, I just can't figure him out. С местоимением фразовый глагол разрывается — figure him out, а не figure out him.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite in casual spoken English, using a contraction and a phrasal verb with 'put': We will postpone the meeting until Friday.
exercises.answer: We'll put off the meeting until Friday.
accept: We'll put the meeting off until Friday.
We're putting off the meeting until Friday.
We're putting the meeting off until Friday.
We'll put off the meeting till Friday.
We'll put the meeting off till Friday.
We're going to put off the meeting until Friday.
We're going to put the meeting off until Friday.
We're going to put off the meeting till Friday.
We're going to put the meeting off till Friday.
We're putting off the meeting till Friday.
We're putting the meeting off till Friday.
exercises.explanation_ru: Разговорный регистр заменяет латинский глагол (postpone) фразовым (put off) и сокращает will: We'll put off the meeting. Дополнение-существительное может стоять и между частями глагола: put the meeting off.

points.title_en: Nuanced quantification, approximation and vague language
points.summary_ru: На высоком уровне количество в английском выражается не только числами. Quite a few значит «довольно много», а не «немного»; not a few — литота с тем же смыслом. Приблизительность передают about, around, roughly, in the region of, upwards of («более»), or so, give or take, суффикс -odd (twenty-odd people — «двадцать с лишним») и a good + единица времени (a good hour — «добрый час»). Эмфатические обороты no fewer than и as many as подчёркивают, что число велико, а as few as и as little as — что мало; по исчисляемости они выбираются так же, как many и much. Партитивы тоже различают оттенки: the lion's share (бо́льшая часть), a handful of (горстка), next to nothing (почти ничего), all but (почти: all but impossible), the better part of (почти весь: the better part of an hour). Расплывчатые выражения уместны в речи и журналистике, но в отчёте требуют уточнения цифрой. В разговоре точность размывают намеренно: -ish (fortyish), sort of / kind of, and stuff / and things, or something, or whatever — это признак непринуждённости, а не небрежности; stuff при этом неисчисляемое и -s не берёт.
forms: quite a few / not a few (= довольно много) ↔ a few / few
upwards of / in the region of / give or take + число; twenty-odd; a good hour
no fewer than / as many as + исчисляемое; as much as / as little as + неисчисляемое
the lion's share of / a handful of / next to nothing
all but + прилагательное (= почти)
examples: The repairs will cost in the region of $5,000.
The drive takes three hours, give or take.
Rooms start at as little as $40 a night.
A handful of fans flew in from Europe.
Tickets sold out in an hour or so.
Quite a few guests left before the speeches.
points.ru_interference: Русские «довольно много» и «несколько» легко спутать, поэтому quite a few понимают как «немного» — а это «довольно много». Эмфатические обороты выбирают по привычке, а не по исчисляемости: неверно «as much as 50,000 people» → верно «as many as 50,000 people»; а к -odd добавляют -s: неверно «thirty-odds» → верно «thirty-odd».

exercises.prompt: 'Not a few investors have privately questioned the valuation.' What does this mean?
options: A fair number of investors have questioned it.
Hardly any investors have questioned it.
Only a handful of investors have questioned it.
Almost all the investors have questioned it.
exercises.explanation_ru: Not a few — литота: «немало», то есть довольно много. Русскоязычные читают not как «ни одного» или a few как «немного» и получают противоположный смысл. Almost all — преувеличение: not a few говорит о заметном числе, но не о большинстве.

exercises.prompt: The survey received ___ 4,000 responses, far more than expected.
exercises.explanation_ru: No fewer than + число подчёркивает, что его много: «ни много ни мало 4000». No more than и as few as, наоборот, подчёркивают, что мало, а barely — «едва»: все три противоречат far more than expected.

exercises.prompt: We spent ___ a year negotiating the contract — eleven months, to be exact.
exercises.explanation_ru: The better part of — «бо́льшая часть, почти весь»: одиннадцать месяцев из двенадцати. Upwards of и a good значат «больше» и «не меньше года», no less than — «целый год, не меньше»: все три противоречат eleven months.

exercises.prompt: Tourism accounts for ___ of the island's income: almost 80 percent last year.
exercises.explanation_ru: The lion's share — «львиная доля», бо́льшая часть: с 80 процентами согласуется только она. A fraction — «малая доля», next to nothing — «почти ничего», а a handful (горстка) говорят только об исчисляемом: a handful of fans, но не a handful of income.

exercises.prompt: We waited a ___ (an adjective meaning 'at least, not less than'; not 'full') hour before anyone came to help.
exercises.answer: good
accept: solid
exercises.explanation_ru: A good + единица времени или расстояния — «добрый, целый, не меньше»: a good hour, a good ten miles. В американской речи в том же значении говорят и a solid hour.

exercises.prompt: Finding a parking spot downtown on a Saturday is ___ (= almost; two words) impossible.
exercises.answer: all but
accept: next to
close to
exercises.explanation_ru: All but + прилагательное — «почти»: all but impossible. Next to impossible значит то же самое.

exercises.prompt: The festival drew as much as 50,000 people.
exercises.answer: The festival drew as many as 50,000 people.
exercises.explanation_ru: Эмфатическое as many as стоит перед исчисляемым числом (людей), as much as — перед суммами и неисчисляемым (as much as $50,000).

exercises.prompt: Twenty-odds guests turned up for the reunion.
exercises.answer: Twenty-odd guests turned up for the reunion.
exercises.explanation_ru: Суффикс -odd («с лишним») присоединяется к числу через дефис и не берёт -s: twenty-odd guests.

exercises.prompt: The festival attracted ___ (formal: more than) 60,000 visitors, roughly ___ (= two times) as many as last year. Tickets sold out in an hour ___ (= approximately). The ___ (= the biggest part) of visitors came from out of state, though a ___ (= a small number) of fans flew in from Europe.
exercises.explanation_ru: Upwards of / in excess of — «более чем», twice as many as — кратность, an hour or so — «около часа», the lion's share — «львиная доля», a handful of — «горстка».

exercises.prompt: Как сказать по-английски: «Он почти ничего не заплатил за эту картину»?
options: He paid next to nothing for the painting.
He paid near to nothing for the painting.
He paid almost anything for the painting.
He paid nearly nothing at all of money for the painting.
exercises.explanation_ru: Next to nothing — «почти ничего». Near to nothing — калька, almost anything значит «почти что угодно», а nearly nothing at all of money — нагромождение.

exercises.prompt: Voice message: 'Hi, it's Dana. Running a bit late — I'll be there at seven-___ (casual 'about seven'). The client meeting went on for three hours ___ (casual 'approximately'), and we talked about budgets, hiring ___ (casual 'and similar things'). It was ___ (casual hedge = 'a little') exhausting, to be honest. Grab me a sandwich ___ (casual 'or something similar'), would you?'
exercises.explanation_ru: В живой речи точность намеренно размывают: seven-ish — «около семи», or so — «примерно», and stuff / and things — «и всё такое» (stuff неисчисляемое, stuffs — ошибка), kind of / sort of — смягчение, or something — «или что-то в этом роде». В отчёте или письме те же места требуют цифры и точного перечня.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite in a formal style, using 'in the region of': The new stadium will cost about $400 million.

The new stadium will cost in the region of 400 million dollars.
exercises.explanation_ru: In the region of + число — формальное «порядка, около»: так пишут в отчётах и новостях. About и around нейтральны, а or so и -ish — разговорные. Предлог in и артикль the в обороте обязательны: in region of и on the region of невозможны.
